locator: radius-limited INTERIOR minimum cross-section of the forearm tube (R_MAX 45 mm excludes the thumb column; the cut-plane band z <= cap+12 mm is excluded because the stump is CUT and its cap ring is otherwise always the global minimum), metric = convex-hull area, centre = pooled centroid of the minimum basin
selection_rule: MOST PROXIMAL interior local minimum of the smoothed section-area profile (window +-20 slabs)
why_not_global_minimum: the palm is flattened (~90 x 25 mm -> ~2090 mm2) and is marginally SMALLER than the round wrist (~55 x 38 mm -> ~2110 mm2), so a pure global minimum-area rule lands in the palm; the wrist is the first minimum after the forearm taper
note: CON-6 forbids the forearm cut-plane centre; the Stage-4B WRIST_R IS exactly that (its own log: '-1.9 mm from the forearm cap'), so it was NOT reused. The locator used here independently reproduces the already-accepted Stage-3 wrist level to <1 mm.

cross_file_verification.verdict: world geometry is bit-comparable; the residual is float32 mesh storage rounding from re-expressing local coordinates, not a geometric change

P0_STYLE_FINDING.what: the Stage-4B TEMP rig's WRIST_R head sits ON the forearm cut plane: its z (0.277349 m) equals the mesh bounding-box minimum (0.276016 m), and the Stage-4B run log itself reports 'narrowest cross-section at -1.9 mm from the forearm cap'
P0_STYLE_FINDING.why_it_matters: CON-6 says to prefer reusing the Stage-4B WRIST_R joint centre AND forbids using the forearm cut-plane centre.  Those two clauses conflict, because on this asset they are the same point.  The hard prohibition was treated as controlling.
P0_STYLE_FINDING.consequence: the two differ by ~58 mm along the arm
P0_STYLE_FINDING.secondary: the Stage-3 wrist_narrowest_z = 0.343 m was itself derived from a slice with only n = 8 vertices (neighbours n = 19..27); the level it names is nevertheless confirmed here by an independent robust locator
P0_STYLE_FINDING.requires: Human Review acknowledgement -- the Stage-4B skeleton's WRIST_R (and hence its 201 mm wrist->palm bone) is anatomically wrong.  It does not affect the RSSF joint-angle validation, which is measured entirely on the fingers.
